title: Decide the daemon runtime: pinned Node in a signed .app
body:
## Decision needed
Which runtime the core daemon runs on once Electron is gone.

**Recommended:** a pinned official Node binary inside a signed `Agent Wrangler.app` bundle, with `dist/` beside it. The bundle stays a `.app` so macOS privacy grants (microphone, Automation) keep attaching to a stable signed identity (#56), and session hosts keep running from an APFS clone of it.

Alternatives: a Node single-executable application (complicates esbuild output and signing for no gain), or Homebrew `node` (unpinned, breaks on `brew upgrade`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Choice recorded in `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4 and on this issue.

## Effort
XS: a decision, not code.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4, D1.

title: Decide how the LAN listener gets TLS
body:
## Decision needed
How browsers on other devices get a trusted HTTPS connection to the daemon. TLS is required on the LAN: plain http on a LAN IP is not a secure context (clipboard, notifications and microphone stop working) and exposes the device credential.

**Recommended:** the daemon creates a local CA and a server certificate (SANs: `<host>.local` and current LAN IPs). Each device trusts the CA once through a configuration profile. A user-supplied certificate and key is supported as an alternative.

Out of scope either way: public certificates that need a public name, tunnels, relays.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Choice recorded in `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §8 and on this issue, including how iOS and macOS clients install trust.

## Effort
XS: a decision.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §8, D2.

title: Decide how notifications reach James when no browser tab is open
body:
## Decision needed
Electron `Notification` goes away with Electron. Open tabs can use the Web Notifications API, but something has to cover the case where no tab is open.

**Recommended:** Discord when remote control is enabled; otherwise an `osascript display notification` on the daemon host. No native helper app.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Choice recorded in `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6 and on this issue.

## Effort
XS: a decision.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6, D3.

title: Decide whether a menu-bar presence survives Electron's retirement
body:
## Decision needed
The menu-bar item (attention count, agent list, Open/Stop) is Electron's `Tray`. A Node daemon cannot draw one.

**Recommended:** drop it; the browser tab title and favicon carry the attention count. Revisit a small Swift helper only if it is missed in practice.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Choice recorded in `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6 and on this issue.

## Effort
XS: a decision.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6, D4.

title: Run every Claude conversation in a session host and remove the in-process path
body:
## Purpose
Once the core is a daemon, an update restarts it. Conversations must not end when that happens. Hosted sessions already survive; in-process ones (`experimental.sessionHosts` is still `false` by default) do not.

## Scope
- Make session hosts the only execution mode for Claude conversations; remove the setting and the in-process runner path.
- Migrate any in-process conversation at upgrade: resumable, not silently lost.
- Update quit semantics and README where they mention in-process sessions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every new Claude conversation runs in a host; there is no setting to turn that off.
- [ ] A restart of the core never ends a Claude conversation.
- [ ] Lifecycle integration suite green.

## Effort
M: the host path already ships (#14, #15); this removes the alternative and its tests. Uncertainty: low, unless the #15 soak finds host bugs.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4, slice 1.

title: Add a principal, request context, central authorization and audit attribution
body:
## Purpose
Establish the boundary future accounts would need, without building accounts. Every action knows who is acting and through what, and passes one authorization check.

## Scope
- `Principal` (one fixed `local-owner`), `RequestContext {principal, via, deviceId?, connectionId?}`.
- `authorize(ctx, action, resource?)` called by the pane hosts' dispatch, the control backend and the remote service before `SessionActions`/orchestration calls. Single-user policy: allow the owner, deny anything else.
- Discord `authorizedUserIds` map to the owner principal; CLI and the app acting on its own get `via: 'cli' | 'daemon'`.
- Audit records principal and `via` on every mutating action (ids only, no content).
- Document host-wide vs potentially user-owned settings (plan §9 table).

Non-goals: login, registration, roles, teams.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No mutating path reaches `SessionActions` without a `RequestContext` and an `authorize` call (test enumerates entry points).
- [ ] Connection and device ids are never used as identity.
- [ ] Audit lines carry principal and `via`.

## Effort
M: mostly threading a parameter through existing entry points. Uncertainty: moderate on how many call sites `SessionActions` has outside the three dispatchers.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §9, slice 2.

title: Move secrets to the Keychain with a one-time migration from safeStorage
body:
## Purpose
`safeStorage` exists only in Electron. The daemon needs secrets without it, and the migration has to run while Electron can still decrypt the old file.

## Scope
- A `HostSecrets` over the login Keychain (`security -i` with commands on stdin, so a secret never appears in argv).
- On first run of a build that has it, the Electron app decrypts `secrets.json` and writes each entry to the Keychain, then removes the file.
- Discord bot token and local-endpoint keys both covered.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Existing secrets survive the upgrade; `secrets.json` is gone afterwards.
- [ ] No secret in argv, logs or settings.
- [ ] This ships at least one release before Electron is removed.

## Effort
S: one small adapter plus a migration. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4, slice 3.

title: Implement HostServices for plain Node
body:
## Purpose
`createApp` takes only `HostServices`; the daemon needs an implementation with no Electron.

## Scope
- Settings, state, logging, data dirs over the existing `JsonStore`/`JsonSettings`.
- Keychain secrets (from the secrets slice).
- `dialogs`, `notify`, `shell`, `clipboard` delegate to a client broker (connection-scoped prompts slice) with non-interactive defaults when no client applies.
- `caffeinate` for the power assertion; a timer-gap sleep watcher for wake.
- PATH fix-up as `toolPath.ts` does.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `createApp(createNodeHost(...))` starts under plain `node` in a test with a temp data dir.
- [ ] No import of `electron` under the new host.

## Effort
M: most members are thin wrappers of code that already exists. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4 and §6, slice 4.

title: Route prompts, toasts and navigation to the client that asked
body:
## Purpose
`HostDialogs` and `WorkbenchSurface` are app-wide singletons. With several browsers, a confirmation started on a phone must appear on that phone, and a row click must open the conversation in the tab that clicked. The prototype showed both going to the Electron window instead.

## Scope
- Carry `RequestContext.connectionId` into `dialogs.*`, `flash` and `surface.show*` calls made while handling a client message.
- A `shell` channel carries `prompt` (confirm/pick/input, with a request id), `toast` and `navigate`.
- A prompt whose connection drops resolves as cancelled.
- Work the app starts by itself (notifications, dictation setup, quit) broadcasts a notice and takes the non-interactive default; it never waits on an invisible modal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With two clients, a confirm or pick started by one appears only on that one.
- [ ] Row click, new conversation and delegation open in the originating client.
- [ ] Tests cover disconnect mid-prompt and app-initiated prompts.

## Effort
L: about 25 `surface` call sites and every dialog-driven action. **Significant uncertainty:** some actions may need redesign rather than threading; split if so.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §7.3, slice 5.

title: Serve the web workbench: assets, CSP, loopback listener, login link and device cookie
body:
## Purpose
The production version of the prototype's HTTP side (`src/electron/webPrototype.ts`).

## Scope
- Listen on `127.0.0.1` only (the LAN is a separate slice).
- Hashed asset names with `immutable` caching; HTML `no-store`, fresh nonce per request; CSP as a header including `connect-src` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- `Host` allowlist (DNS rebinding) and `Origin` checks.
- Loopback login: `aw web open` mints a single-use, short-lived link that becomes an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` device cookie bound to the owner principal.
- Security headers as in the prototype.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Foreign Host gets 421, foreign Origin 403, missing credential 401; a used login link cannot be reused.
- [ ] Only `dist/webview` is reachable as static content.
- [ ] Tests for guards and link expiry.

## Effort
M: the prototype covers half. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §8 and §10, slice 6.

title: Implement the browser WebSocket API: handshake, reconnect, dedupe and flow control
body:
## Purpose
A connection protocol good enough for phones on flaky Wi-Fi, carrying today's pane envelopes.

## Scope
- `ws` package (bundled) with permessage-deflate, replacing the prototype codec.
- `shell.hello {protocol, build}`; build mismatch makes the client reload.
- Reconnect with backoff and re-`ready` instead of a page reload; conversation `ready` carries the session key.
- Client-generated `commandId` on mutating messages; per-device result cache (10 min) so a resend after a drop does not act twice.
- Per-connection buffered-bytes ceiling.
- Table snapshot coalesced per connection (at most 1/s, 1/10 s while hidden).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Killing the socket mid-stream and reconnecting restores the table and the same conversation without reload.
- [ ] A `send` resent with the same `commandId` is delivered once.
- [ ] Measured table traffic per idle client drops well below the prototype's ~11 KB/s.

## Effort
L: protocol plus client shim plus tests. Uncertainty: moderate on the reconnect edge cases in the conversation pane.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §7, slice 7.

title: Package the daemon runtime as a signed .app with pinned Node
body:
## Purpose
The daemon, session hosts and remote daemon need a runtime that is not Electron.

## Scope
- Build a signed `Agent Wrangler.app` containing a pinned Node binary and `dist/`, signed with the local certificate.
- Session-host runtime cloning (`sessionHostRuntime.ts`) and the remote daemon run `node` from the clone instead of `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`.
- `bin/aw` uses the bundled Node.
- While Electron coexists, both can be in the bundle.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `npm run app:install` produces the bundle; hosts started from it survive a reinstall.
- [ ] Privacy grants persist across rebuilds.

## Effort
L: packaging and signing are fiddly. **Uncertainty:** high until D1 is settled and the first signed build works.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4, slice 8.

title: Run the application core in a LaunchAgent daemon
body:
## Purpose
The core outlives every window and browser, and starts without one.

## Scope
- Daemon entry: Node host, `createApp`, `start()`, control socket, web server.
- LaunchAgent `com.hammonjj.agentwrangler.core`: `RunAtLoad` when Open at login is on, `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`; single instance by label plus socket probe; manifest in `run/`.
- `aw daemon start|stop|stop --all|status`; quit policy as today (hosts keep running).
- Install and update: bootout plus bootstrap; hosts reattach through `HostSupervisor.scan`.
- Power assertion and wake handling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With no browser and no window, agents run, approvals reach Discord, and `aw` works.
- [ ] Daemon update and crash leave hosted conversations running and reattached.
- [ ] Closing every browser does not stop the daemon.

## Effort
L: lifecycle patterns exist (remote daemon, hosts). Uncertainty: moderate.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4, slice 9.

title: Make the Electron window a client of the daemon's web UI
body:
## Purpose
One UI code path during the migration. Electron stops owning the core and becomes a browser.

## Scope
- Electron main no longer calls `createApp`; it ensures the daemon is running and opens a `BrowserWindow` on the loopback URL with a loopback credential.
- Remove the IPC bridge, `aw://` serving and preload bridge from the window path (keep only what the window shell needs).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The window and a browser tab show the same state and both can act.
- [ ] Quitting the window leaves the daemon and agents running.

## Effort
M: mostly deletion plus a URL load. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §11, slice 10.

title: Make multiple clients converge on conversation and approval state
body:
## Purpose
Several browsers for the same user see the same truth, and an approval answered anywhere disappears everywhere.

## Scope
- Integration tests with two or more simulated clients: both see a pending permission; one approves; the other's card clears; the other's late approval gets `stale` and a toast.
- Same for questions and plans, and for a Discord press while clients are connected.
- Reconnect after missed updates converges to current state.
- View state (selection, scroll, split, drafts) stays per client.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The scenarios above pass in CI.
- [ ] No approval path exists that bypasses `SessionActions`.

## Effort
M: mostly tests; fixes where they fail. Uncertainty: moderate.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §7.2 and §8, slice 11.

title: Build the web app shell: routes, modals, toasts and focus management
body:
## Purpose
The workbench bundle becomes an app shell that works without a native window around it.

## Scope
- Routes: Agents, Conversation, Missions, Analytics, Preferences (URL-addressable, back button works).
- Above a breakpoint, today's split; below it, one pane at a time with back navigation. The shell sizes off the viewport; panes keep sizing off themselves.
- In-page modal host for `prompt` (confirm/pick/input), replacing the palette window; toast host.
- Focus trap and restore for modals; focus to heading on route change.
- Keep the existing vanilla TypeScript bundles; no framework rewrite (plan §5).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every flow that used the palette or a native dialog works in a browser.
- [ ] Keyboard-only use reaches every route and modal.

## Effort
L. Uncertainty: moderate.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §5, slice 12.

title: Make the table, conversation and composer work on a phone
body:
## Purpose
Mobile browsers are first-class clients. The prototype showed the split at 390 px gives two unusable 180 px panes.

## Scope
- Stacked single-pane layout from the shell.
- Conversation narrow mode (a `ResizeObserver` class like the table's): composer, permission/question/plan cards, markdown tables, code blocks and diffs at 360 px.
- 44 px touch targets; no hover-only affordances; safe-area insets.
- Verify on iOS Safari and Android Chrome.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a phone: find an agent, read its conversation, send a message, answer a permission, question and plan.
- [ ] No horizontal page scroll at 360 px.

## Effort
L. **Significant uncertainty** in conversation ergonomics; may split per surface.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §5, slice 13.

title: Serve Preferences, Missions and Analytics as routes of the web app
body:
## Purpose
The Preferences window and the other secondary surfaces become routes of the one document.

## Scope
- Port the preferences bundle (settings, orchestration, local endpoints, routing) into a route over the same WebSocket.
- Missions and Analytics reachable as routes, usable at narrow widths.
- Setting actions (`runSettingAction`) work from the browser.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every setting can be read and changed from a browser, including on a phone.
- [ ] No second window is needed for anything.

## Effort
M. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §5, slice 14.

title: Add an opt-in LAN listener with TLS
body:
## Purpose
Let browsers on other devices on the home network reach the daemon, safely and only on request.

## Scope
- Preferences opt-in, off by default; shows the bound addresses.
- TLS per D2 (local CA and server certificate, or user-supplied).
- `Host` allowlist extended to the bound names; `Secure` cookies.
- Document LAN deployment assumptions: trusted network, firewall, no port forwarding.

Non-goals: public URLs, port forwarding, relays.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Off by default; nothing listens on a non-loopback interface until enabled.
- [ ] A phone that trusts the CA loads the workbench over HTTPS with clipboard and notifications working.

## Effort
M. Uncertainty: moderate (certificate trust on iOS).

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §8, slice 15.

title: Pair devices, list them and revoke them
body:
## Purpose
Remote browsers need credentials that can be provisioned without an Electron window and taken away.

## Scope
- Pairing from the loopback browser or `aw web pair`: QR code and short code, 5-minute single use.
- 256-bit device credential; only its hash stored (`devices.json`, 0600) with name, created and last seen.
- Device list in Preferences and `aw web devices [revoke <id>]`; revoking closes that device's connections at once.
- Rate limits and lockout on pairing attempts; upload caps.
- Audit pairing, login, revocation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A phone pairs by QR without touching the Mac's keyboard beyond starting pairing.
- [ ] A revoked device is disconnected and cannot reconnect.
- [ ] Brute-forcing a pairing code is locked out.

## Effort
L. Uncertainty: moderate.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §8, slice 16.

title: Fold the Discord remote daemon into the core daemon
body:
## Purpose
One LaunchAgent, one feed. With secrets in the Keychain, Discord also stops waiting for the app to be opened after a reboot.

## Scope
- Run `RemoteControlService` inside the core daemon; remove the separate LaunchAgent and its socket after migrating.
- Collapse the app-feed/own-feed switch.
- Keep the audit log, allowlist and stale checks unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a reboot, Discord works with no window or browser opened.
- [ ] No duplicate cards across the migration.

## Effort
M. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §4, slice 17.

title: Upload and download files and browse host folders from the browser
body:
## Purpose
A remote client's file paths are not daemon-host paths. Files need explicit transfer, and folder selection needs a host-side browser.

## Scope
- Upload: HTTP POST (Origin check plus custom header) into a per-conversation staging directory on the host; the message references the host path. Images stay inline.
- Download: `GET /files/...` limited to session working directories, worktrees and transcript directories; audited.
- Folder browser for New Conversation: known projects first, then a tree under `$HOME`, clearly labelled as paths on the host.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dropping a non-image file in a remote browser attaches it; the agent can read it on the host.
- [ ] No client-supplied path is ever treated as a host path.
- [ ] Downloads outside the allowlist are refused.

## Effort
M. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6, slice 18a.

title: Replace host-local actions with browser alternatives
body:
## Purpose
Open in editor, Show in Finder and Resume in Terminal act on the host's screen, which a remote user cannot see.

## Scope
- Read-only file view and diff view in the browser for `openFile` and mission diffs.
- Resume/Release from a remote client shows and copies `claude --resume <id>`.
- Reveal shows and copies the host path, or offers download.
- For a loopback client, keep "Open on this Mac" variants, labelled as acting on the host.
- External links open in the clicking browser.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No remote action opens a window on the host unasked.
- [ ] Every former host-local action has a remote behaviour.

## Effort
M. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6, slice 18b.

title: Notify through the browser and record dictation in the browser
body:
## Purpose
Notifications and dictation are tied to the host's screen and microphone today.

## Scope
- Web Notifications in open tabs (secure context) with a deep link to the session; fallback per D3 when no tab is open.
- Dictation: record with `MediaRecorder` in the browser, upload the audio, transcribe with the existing whisper pipeline on the daemon. A loopback client may keep host-mic recording.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A finished agent notifies a phone with the tab open; tapping opens that session.
- [ ] Dictation from a phone produces text in its composer.

## Effort
M. Uncertainty: moderate (mobile audio formats).

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §6, slice 18c.

title: Retire Electron
body:
## Purpose
One supported runtime. Electron is removed once the browser covers what the window did.

## Scope
- Pass the retirement checklist in `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §11, in a local browser and on a paired phone.
- Delete `src/electron/`, the preload, the `aw://` scheme, the palette and preferences windows, the tray (per D4), Electron and electron-builder.
- The `.app` is the Node daemon bundle; opening it opens the browser on the loopback login link.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Checklist passed and recorded on this issue.
- [ ] No `electron` dependency or import remains.
- [ ] Install, update and restart keep agents running.

## Effort
M: mostly deletion once parity exists. Uncertainty: low, given its blockers.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md` §11, slice 19.

title: Update docs for the browser-only architecture
body:
## Purpose
Docs say what the product is after the migration.

## Scope
- README and product principles: execution host vs browser client, loopback default, LAN opt-in scope, no public exposure, future accounts.
- CLAUDE.md: commands, restart rules (daemon, not app), install.
- Architecture docs: mark superseded sections; setup and troubleshooting (pairing, certificates, daemon status).
- Remove the prototype notes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No doc describes Electron as the runtime.
- [ ] Setup from scratch on a new Mac and a phone works from the README alone.

## Effort
S. Uncertainty: low.

Spec: `docs/plans/browser-workbench.md`, slice 20.
